messages:
maria_zhou: Quick proposal — we should standardize a ‘golden path’ for instrumentation that enforces low-cardinality primitives + a small set of high-cardinality opt-ins. Goal: reliable cost attribution + bounded telemetry volume.

sam_kapoor: +1. can you sketch required attributes?

maria_zhou: minimal set: service, env, route, customer_id (hashed), request_type. everything else should be an optional metadata blob. cardinality cap: no more than 3 customer-facing freeform keys per span.

james: how do we enforce? SDK lint + ingest gates?

maria_zhou: exactly. 3 layers: 1) SDK lint warnings on dev machines; 2) CI/PR blocker rule that rejects new high-cardinality keys in open-source SDKs; 3) ingest-side guardrail that drops/labels exceeding keys and emits a governance metric. devops-bot: deploy note: ingest guardrails can be toggled via feature flag.

linh_tran: concern: some partners need rich attributes for billing. opt-in?

maria_zhou: partner opt-in via signed contract + allowlist tenant header. default remains strict. we’ll add a per-tenant attribute quota and explicit billing tag so cost attribution remains exact.

sam_kapoor: sampling interactions? If we sample traces, cost attribution can be biased. want to avoid undercounting heavy tenants.

maria_zhou: plan: sampling decisions must be tenant-aware for billing metrics. two-fold approach: deterministic sampling for billing (1/1 for high value tenants) and statistical sampling for general telemetry. we emit a sampling-weight attribute so queries can reweight.

james: example reweighting snippet?

maria_zhou: ```sql
-- approximate reweighting in analytics
SUM(cost * (1.0 / sampling_probability)) as estimated_cost
WHERE sampling_weight IS NOT NULL
```

linh_tran: rollout path? big migration risk if we change span schema.

maria_zhou: rollout: 1) add SDK lint + warning in nightly builds; 2) announce golden-path and start a 30d migration advisory; 3) enable CI checks blocking new violations; 4) opt-in ingest guardrails in canary region for 2 weeks; 5) global enforcement with a monitoring dashboard and rollback playbook.

sam_kapoor: metric/traces correlation: need stable request_id surface across logs/metrics/spans. propose header X-RD-REQ or use trace_id fallback.

maria_zhou: agree. canonicalize to request_id when present, else trace_id. also include short_trace (first 8 chars) in metrics to reduce join cardinality.

james: what about agent vs proxy instrumentation? android/js/edge SDKs often push raw attrs to the proxy which enriches.

maria_zhou: rule: client SDKs should do lightweight sanitization + hashing of PII, but full attribute canonicalization happens at proxy/ingest to avoid inconsistent SDK behavior. SDKs still enforce local cardinality lint.

linh_tran: alerting for enforcement breakage? we need a quick sight when many spans are being trimmed.

maria_zhou: ingest will emit governance metrics: trimmed_spans_count, trimmed_keys_by_team, top-trimmed-keys. Alerts: sudden spike in trimmed_spans or a tenant > 1% of requests trimmed -> page oncall.

sam_kapoor: love the governance metrics. add a weekly report per-product showing pre/post migration telemetry differences.

maria_zhou: done. also adding a tiny example SDK rule to the repo: ```js
// SDK lint rule pseudocode
if (attribute_name.match(/email|phone|ssn/)) {
  warn("PII detected — hash or remove");
}
if (attribute_cardinality(attribute_name) > 500) {
  error("Too high cardinality for attribute: " + attribute_name);
}
```

devops-bot: FYI: feature flag "ingest.attr-guardrails.v1" created. default=false. owners: @maria_zhou, @sam_kapoor.

james: ok next steps for eng-platform: draft the RFC with the enforcement matrix and migration timeline. I'll pair with @maria_zhou on the governance dashboard mockups.

maria_zhou: thanks — I'll draft the RFC today and tag teams. keeping the golden path narrow is the main tradeoff: slightly less flexibility now for much more predictable cost and attribution. :thumbsup:
